title: Micro-Operator: steplet framework for ad-hoc runbook tasks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight, auditable 'steplet' runtime and UX that lets on-call and support engineers run isolated runbook steps as first-class tasks. Steplets are small, parameterized, idempotent operations (e.g., rotate-credentials, restart-service, rehydrate-cache) that can be executed interactively from the Console or invoked by automation (incident workflows, Slack shortcuts).

MVP goals:
- Define a steplet manifest and ABI that supports typed inputs, output schemas, and safe resource scoping.
- Provide a runtime to execute steplets in sandboxed microcontainers with a per-step audit trail and structured logs.
- Integrate steplet execution into Console runbook UI and the support Slack bot (with approval flow).
- Telemetry: per-step latency/cost, success/failure reasons, retry counts, and SLO metrics.
- Safety: dry-run capability, required-approvals for sensitive steplets, KMS-wrapped secrets, and RBAC enforcement.

Architecture decisions and trade-offs:
- Chosen runtime: lightweight microcontainer sandbox (sided against WASM for MVP due to existing tooling and quicker ability to reuse internal container images). Revisiting WASM in Q3 for cold-start improvements.
- Execution model: synchronous for interactive runs, asynchronous task record + webhook for automation. This keeps Console UX responsive while allowing long-running ops.
- Manifest format: YAML with a small schema (inputs, outputs, permissions, runtime hints). Using YAML keeps authoring accessible to SREs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
1) Author a steplet manifest and store in repo under ops/steplets/ with reviewable PR.
2) Run a steplet from Console: prompt for inputs, present dry-run, require approval if marked sensitive.
3) Execution produces an immutable audit event with logs, exit code, and structured output visible in Console and exportable to incident timeline.
4) Slack shortcut runs steplet with ephemeral approval flow and returns structured result.
5) Telemetry emits metrics to telemetry-ops namespace for dashboard and alerting.

Open questions:
- How granular should RBAC be (per-step vs per-namespace)? Proposed: per-step role bindings for sensitive ops, namespace-level default for routine tasks.
- Secret handling for steplets that need DB creds: use envelope + KMS; plan to integrate with existing KMS work (see dependencies).

Artifacts and links:
- Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/steplet-framework
- Prototype branch & PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/1823
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b-steplet-mockups
- Related runbook patterns: https://wiki.internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/ad-hoc-ops
